notes.title: Post-Gamescom Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

 

Ever since coming back from Gamescom we’ve been working on the next batch of changes to Green Again. With Sproutlings are going to Tokyo Game Show soon as part of our publisher Slug Disco, I think this is a good time to polish the game a bit more for our next event appearance.

 

The focus of this update is to make the gameplay more fluid and intuitive, with a variety of optimizations and changes to the UI and game flow. There’s also a number of fixes implemented. See below for the full changelog:

 

Added "no materials" icon for buildings which are missing materials to finish construction

Growing seasons of current crop are shown in the crop switch panel

Reduced power consumption of some buildings

Update season changed tooltip when changing language

Made faster and fastest game speed settings a bit faster

Improved tutorial item pacing, changed tutorial order so panning tutorial is not skipped

Fixed loreleaf monolith spawning in a ring of cliffs occasionally

Fixed some localization bugs

Fixed pods tutorial message icons

Fixed construction costs being added to worker inventories twice

Fixed bug causing crops to be shown as harvestable when they aren't yet

Fixed a bug in quest generation timing

notes.title: June Round-Up (New Update!)🌳
notes.notes:
Heya Sproutling fans!
 

Green Again got a major update with the new Forge Zone back in March, and it’s about time for another big one! The Lore Tree has been introduced to the game to give the Sproutlings even more support on their terraforming endeavours. In our June monthly round-up, we'll be covering this new upgrade system in detail. 


The Lore Tree
A currency called Loreleaves can be earned in each world playthrough by completing and replaying levels, achieving objectives, growing your settlement, or collecting Loreleaf monoliths. You can then use these Loreleaves to unlock upgrades on the Lore Tree, ranging from boosting farm production to buffing buildings and Sproutlings!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/56fa3665a336808d9570554681b51612ffaf9002.png"]

The Lore Tree applies its effects across all zones in the same save file, and does not reset upon starting a new game in a different zone (unlike the previous tech tree). This should make each run easier and more satisfying as you accumulate rewards over time. It can also be accessed from either the world map or mid-game to be reset anytime, allowing you to customize your strategies whenever you like.

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/8ec120e27202633a40b7902972b002363953b923.png"]

Aside from the Lore Tree, this update also introduced a variety of decorations and other changes to freshen up your settlements. You can find the full change log at the end of this blog post.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/5e9949bee854e5f9ed445866e0767cc6ac25036b.png"]

Note: Older save files might not be compatible with this latest version. We recommend starting a new save on the new patch.



What's Next?
We’d like to add more upgrades and customizations to Green Again to increase gameplay variety. There are plans for prebuilt base structures that give players a head start every game, though this will something to work on later. Right now, we’ll be focusing on consolidating the Lore Tree system with further balancing and expansions in the upcoming patches.

 



The Lore Tree is now ripe for harvest. Check it out in Green Again’s demo and let us know what you think! Your feedback would be really appreciated on how we shape the Lore Tree in the future. Join and follow us on Twitter, YouTube and TikTok to share your thoughts and get the latest news of Green Again!




Change log:
Added loreleaves which can be used to unlock lore tree gift upgrades

Added several lore tree gifts

Added various loreleaf objectives

Added loreleaf monoliths

Moved some of the upgrades from tech tree to lore tree

Added willow, reeds and three different mushroom decorations

Added new oak tree art

Fixed junkyard decoration card size

Updated recycler generation, starting recycler count should be more consistent

notes.title: May Round-Up (Demo Update!)🌱
notes.notes:
Hi Sproutling fans!

Summer is here! The warm weather is perfect for our Sproutlings to ramp up their farming and stock up on food and electricity for later in the year. To aid their terraforming endeavours, we just dropped a new patch for the demo. Let’s see what the Sproutlings are getting in this update!

New Demo Update!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/63d6f3c5e18385700e21f62089e934d556fb7b1f.png
The biggest gameplay change in this patch is the new decoration unlock system. Now certain decorations can only be unlocked in specific zones, and the unlocked decorations will carry over to different maps within the same world playthrough. We have also tuned down the fires in the Forge Zone and made them more forgiving. You can find the full change log below 👇

Change log:

 Added new decoration unlock system, each zone has several related decoration unlockables
 Adjusted fire tuning, less punishing fire spread in Forge
 Fields which don't meet the soil requirement of the swap target crop become empty, a warning is shown on UI if the soil is insufficient
 Some messages (e.g. drones) are shown as tutorial messages on the left when the tutorial is active
 Sprinkler description now mentions revealing fogged areas
 Fixed some string errors
 Fixed power recalculation bug when save is reloaded
 Fixed uncaptured and fogged reactors shown in power overlay
 Fixed buggy decoration repair, workers repeatedly walking to damaged decorations
 Fixed auto-pause UI elements unpausing the game even if it had been paused before opening them
 Improved crop switch panel positioning and visibility over other UI elements
 Drone spawning in Town is now linked to player progress

	
Indie Assemble
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/76695c647df7141a4812bf21ad4e5880c707c287.png
Earlier this month, the Sproutlings worked diligently to showcase Green Again at Indie Assemble, a massive indie games Steam event with an extensive collection from around the world. With over 1,000 games from more than 600 development studios, it was the perfect occasion to explore Steam’s vast library of indie games. 


Let us know what you think about the new changes to Green Again, and please look forward to more content coming to the Game. For more news on Green Again, follow us on Twitter, YouTube and TikTok. See you next month!

notes.title: Forge Zone Demo Update ⚙️🤖
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=KbZIuDsASOI;full][/previewyoutube]
Greetings Sproutling Fans!

Spring is here and so is our first big demo update in 2025 – new map, new challenges and new upgrades! Let’s check out all the new content in Green Again!

The Forge Zone
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/bc5ced64726fd30b24af760074c15ea66ab2fc57.png
Introducing the Forge Zone, a brand-new biome with new tiles, new obstacles and new buildings. This will be the biggest challenge so far for our dear Sproutlings… Do they have what it takes to bring nature back to these lands plagued by malfunctioning robots?

New Threats
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/b30d644bfb777c74bca8dbb006ce8fd82b62aa34.png
Bot factories and foundries can be found across the new Forge Zone, imposing new challenges to your settlements. New drones emerge from bot factories to roam the map and harass the Sproutlings; foundries ignite wildfires that spread across the map, laying waste to your buildings and crops.

New Buildings and Tech
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/eb8c86517e26e3030cf5b037de43cc7f74d674df.png
To combat the new threats, the Sproutlings now has updated buildings and technology. Sprinkler towers can be used for both watering the crops and suppressing fires. New upgrades are also available to defeat the drones and boost production. 

And of course, the Forge Zone isn't the only thing being added to Green Again. We've also introduced various additions to other parts of the game. You can find the full patch notes below for all the details of the update!

Join us on Discord, YouTube, Twitter and TikTok to get the latest news on Green Again, and share with us any feedback you have on our game! 


Changelog:

New Forge zone – the most challenging area featuring new buildings and new tile set
New Fire system – Forge Zone foundries set surrounding tiles on fire; buildings are now flammable; Sproutlings take on the role of firefighters to protect their land
Bot factories spawning new drones with more dynamic drone behavior (they actively harass the colony when aggressive, patrolling between factories)
Sprinkler towers which can be used for both fire protection and watering fields
New objectives and challenges in the junkyard zone
Light tower EMP upgrade makes the light towers much more effective against both jellyfish and shielded drones
Darklight converters upgrade allowing power production at night
New SFX (both in-game and UI)
UI features: "Don't show again" checkbox for tutorial messages, Tooltip delay configuration slider
Misc UI improvements, Bugfixes and optimization

notes.title: Green Again Demo Update 🌿
notes.notes:
Hey again, Sproutling fans! 

We've got a brand new demo update coming your way today, and we're excited to share some of the changes we've made. Shall we dive straight in?

New Blueprint System

Sproutlings have a whole new way to build in this latest update to the demo: new buildings will appear as blueprints, with the surrounding workers carrying materials to the construction site to build the new addition. This will be expanded upon in a future update, so keep an eye out...

UX Updates

It should now be easier than ever to manage your colony with our latest UX updates to the demo: trade buttons can now be held down to avoid repetitive clicking (this also works with shift and ctrl keys), a new borderless fullscreen mode allows for more seamless gameplay, and the objectives list has now been moved to the corner of the screen, to give you a better view of your colony. 

Overlays

Managing your power production, crop growth, and seasons just got even simpler! With new overlays to show your farms and production, you can now see, at-a-glance, how your colony is doing and optimise where needed. Your Sproutlings will thank you.

Of course, we're also including the usual bug and performance fixes, including a more optimised and faster start up time for those of you with multiple save files, in this latest update - check out the full patch notes, below, for all the details! 

As always, don't forget to come join us on Discord, Twitter, or TikTok to chat about the new update, ask any questions, or just show some Sproutling love. 

Changelog

 Optimization of animations, sproutling AI, CPU usage, and improving framerate
 Faster game startup and load game menu opening times even with high amount of save files
 Optimized garbage collection and querying of neighbor tiles
 Improved performance of disabling watchtowers
 Buildings appear as blueprints, sproutlings carry materials to construction site
 Selectable sproutlings and robots, displaying relevant info in inspector
 Unique names for sproutlings
 Overlay views for power production, crops grown, crop seasons and soil fertility
 Lack of water no longer prevents placing a higher level house on a lower level one to upgrade it
 Trade buttons can be held down for faster trading (works with ctrl and shift as well)
 Added borderless fullscreen support (can be toggled in options)
 List of objectives and buttons moved to upper right corner
 Fixed worker task scheduling issues
 Various bugfixes, UI and UX tweaks

notes.title: We're Taking Part in Tacticon 2024 + Free Demo Update!
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/9cfb2cc63b2af8f75453087c0225a00390e81bc1.jpg

Hey again, Sproutling fans! 

We're very excited to share that Green Again is taking part in Tacticon 2024, a digital Steam convetion which seeks to highlight some of the best new & upcoming strategy games and the wonderful gamers that play them! 

The event runs from today (July 18th) to July 22nd, and you can see the full list of all the games included in the celebration here.

Naturally, we wanted to provide an update alongside the event itself, so we've got some new features coming to Green Again, too! You can check out the full changelog below, but shall we take a look at the highlights?

Multi-Swapping and Crop Updates

Crop management just got even easier! You can now choose to change all crops on adjacent fields of the same crop type. This can be toggled on or off so you can customise your experience depending on your playstyle. 
Crops now also provide different amounts of food and a bigger resource yield variety, depending on the crop choice too, and you'll have more tactical crop choices - make sure to use them wisely!

Rainfall

Rainfall will now be an unlockable weather type in the Town Zone, and once unlocked, will mean that your fields are automatically watered during rain. There's a new objective in the Town Zone which is related to restoring rain, so keep an eye out for this when playing! 

Quality of Life Updates

Naturally, there are plenty of Quality of Life changes in this new update, including the ability to scroll, zoom, and interact with the game whilst on the pause screen, lots of new sound effects for workers, robots, and ambience, and a new streamlined experience in the Town Zone map, with ancient buildings now closer together. 

Full changelog: 

 Swap all crops for adjacent fields of the same crop type (can be toggled)
 Crops worth different amount of food, bigger variety of crops' food/coins ratio
 Lots of new sound effects for workers, robots, ambience and more, spatial sounds spawned in the game world
 Rainfall as new unlockable weather in town zone (fields are watered when it's raining)
 Allow scrolling, zooming and interacting with the game while paused
 Moved ancient buildings closer in town zone
 Reduced materials selling value
 Gameplay settings available from main menu, settings UI tweaks, scroll speed setting
 Reduced weeds growth chance on more terraformed maps
 Made housing resource icon more visible

 Made closing all tutorials menu similar to other menus
 Hide bonus labels when hovering over an invalid placement tile
 Fix overly eager homeless warnings when replacing houses
 Separate icons for crops missing prerequisites and those that are unlockable but hasn't been unlocked
 Fix several issues related to tutorial reset and progress
 Fix worker disappearing at unreachable bridge end when building bridge
 Fix creative mode button shown again when reloading a save with unlocked creative
 Fix houses and flaggables leaving non-terraformed spots when cleared while their hex is still within hub radius
 Fix season icons and loading overlay scaling issues
 Fix unlocking creative in one zone unlocking it in other zones
 Fix visible pods button in town zone

 Fix float saving issues related to locale (likely reason for volume settings not being saved for some players)
 Fix workers drawn under buildings when zoomed out

notes.title: We're taking part in Next Fest + an Update!
notes.notes:
This. Is. Not. A. Drill. 
We're taking part in Steam Next Fest! 

[previewyoutube=j92VcW6zfF4;full]TRAILER[/previewyoutube]
We're incredibly excited to be bringing Green Again to a whole new audience, and of course, participating in the event means we had to put a little update together, too - more details on that below! 

Updated Tutorial

Whether you're a new player trying the demo for the first time, or have spent a little more time in Green Again, we've reworked the in-game tutorial to make it easier than ever to hit the ground running and get your colony growing. 
If you've played previously and would like to try the new tutorials (or just need a refresher!), start up a level and head to Settings > Gameplay > Reset Tutorial to experience it from scratch! 

Lighting and Power

During the darker months, Sproutling homes, outposts, and lighting decorations will all require power at night, which you'll now need to provide for using a brand new power system: solar panels and batteries. Place solar panels during the warmer, brighter months in-game to generate power and store it in your batteries for use during these colder seasons to keep your Sproutlings happy! Watchtowers will also require power throughout the whole day, so you'll want to stock up as much as possible to be able to defend your colony. 

New Music 

We've got a swanky new soundtrack in this latest update, written by the incredible Tobi Weiss! We don't want to spoil the joy of discovering it for you, so we'll just say this: new theme music and dynamic tracks which become richer as you expand your colony. You're welcome 🎶

All you have to do to access all these new additions is make sure you've updated to the latest version of the demo - so whether you're joining us from Next Fest or you've been around for a while, there's something new to enjoy 💚 Full changelog is below, but in the meantime, have you spotted our latest livestream? 

[previewyoutube=l7oArC3Ywf4;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Green Again Demo Update!
notes.notes:
Hey there, Sproutling fans! 

We've got an exciting new update for you today, and we're pretty keen to share it...so let's dive straight in, shall we?

[previewyoutube=Ir16DEy_KOw;full][/previewyoutube]

If you're following us on Twitter or TikTok, you might've seen a little teaser last week...Sproutlings have had a makeover! They now have new animations, hairstyles, and facial expressions, which we happen to think makes them even more adorable. 

It's not just the Sproutlings that have had a glow up, though - we've also got a brand new UI for you, with custom elements, a new font, and streamlined functionality to make it easier than ever to manage your Sproutlings (and keep them safe from pesky robots!), and we've spruced up the world map and changed the way zones are generated, so they're now a more circular shape. Fancy, eh?

Of course, with a new look and feel, it only felt right to do a little spring cleaning on how you manage your Sproutling colony; hungry or unhappy Sproutlings will now leave the settlement if they're not getting what they need, so you'll have to rise to the challenge.  
Luckily, higher level housing can now be placed over the lower level ones you might have started out with, so you can keep your decorations in place and upgrade your settlement without forfeiting Sproutling happiness. Phew!

We've also got some bug fixes and minor tweaks coming with this latest update, so you can read the full patch notes below for more information on those. 

As always, don't forget to come join us on Discord, Twitter, or TikTok to chat about the new update, ask any questions, or just show some Sproutling love. 

Changelog:

 Brand new sproutling animations with various hairstyles, facial expressions, idle anims
 New UI with custom elements, font and icons, streamlined some UI functionality
 New world map (planet view with decorative tiles)
 Revised fog, buildings reveal fogged areas in a smooth circular radius
 Zones generated with circular shape (with cliffs at the borders)
 Hungry and unhappy sproutlings leave the settlement
 Higher level houses can be placed over lower level ones
 Variation in decoration costs, more expensive decorations give bigger happiness boost
 Watchtowers shoot light rays towards exposed bots
 Clear tool can be used to remove EMP pod from a tile
 Mapgen data loaded from data file for greater flexibility
 Huge cleanup of codebase to allow smoother updates and better performance
 Fixed various UI bugs
 Fixed loading glitch
 Fixed blinking no water icon on fields
 Misc fixes and economy tweaks

notes.title: Green Again Demo Update
notes.notes:
Hey there, Sproutling fans! 

We've got a new update to the demo for you, just in time for Dinos vs. Robots Fest, which we'll be participating in next week! 

There are some exciting new challenges to look forward to with this latest update, so shall we dive into the highlights?

First up on the agenda: drones. These protective lil bots will now appear during both zones in the demo, and they'll be tasked with defending the Ancient Buildings in the Town Zone, and the Transmitters in the Junkyard. They'll be able to harm your Sproutlings, so you might want to build some watchtowers...

Which brings us to our next point: Sproutling workers that are harmed now become incapacitated, turning them into Soul Seeds which need to be regrown in the aptly named Soul Garden. You'll be able to see your incapacitated workers as a separate stat in-game, so you can keep track of them! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44781286/5daffdef1a48d490dfd2d4047c06547cdb776edd.png
We've also got some updated Sproutling management tools for you, allowing you to choose whether you'd like your Sproutlings to clear or gather from a tile, as well as giving you the option to forbid them from using specific tiles - this will come in handy with those pesky drones on the loose! 

Of course, there are plenty more quality of life and bug fixes, including clearer tracking of food and consumption and production, expanded tutorials covering new topics, and lots more! You can read the full changelog down below. 

If you'd like to give us any feedback, have any questions, or just want to chat about the demo, don't forget to stop by our Discord, Twitter, or TikTok!

Change log:


 New population system: outposts won't consume workers, they have a min. population requirement instead
 Added streamer mode for content creators, disabling CC4 songs
 Replaced rock resource with junk
 Several tweaks made to food calculation, upgrade and structure costs
 Building info panels are updated real-time when resources change
 Fixed camera scrolling and panning overshoot, snappier camera controls
 Using the clear tool continues to apply on/off depending on the first action, making quick clear marking big areas by LMB held down easier
 Tweaks and streamlining of tutorial
 Game preferences are now stored in a separate file
 Building captured state is shown in inspector
 Fixed short blink of zone hexes when loading world view
 Fixed inaccessible ancient buildings causing soft-lock
 House decoration quest works both ways: house placed next to decoration and vice versa
 Pods remain available in junkyard creative mode

notes.title: Winter update, holiday content
notes.notes:
Hi there! Before relaxing and having a little vacation time, a Winter update is due. The update consists of a small bundle of holiday items and various fixes and improvements. Enjoy your holidays and thanks for your support and kindness (and don't forget to wishlist please!)

Changelog:
- Winter holiday content: Festive tree, Snowman, Stashes appear as presents, Worker hats :)
- When selecting clear, resources are shown over collectibles
- Settings for audio and graphics are available from main menu, Improved ultrawide support
- Reduced jellyfish count to four in junkyard zone
- Tweaked decoration unlock sound
- Fixed some description text
- Changed some tutorial texts and events
